newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures narrowly mixed awaiting auction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures narrowly mixed awaiting auction.

text.p: U.S. debt futures were narrowly mixed in early trade as players await Treasury's auction of $12.0 billion in 10-year notes.
"It's your typical auction trade," said John Kadich, futures floor analyst for Dean Witter Futures. "It's whippy in a tight range," he said.
Debt futures started lower but cut their losses to turn mixed in the first half-hour of trade as dealers stepped in to buy up to 4,000 September Treasury bond futures, traders said.
"We're just waiting on the 10-year," a T-bond broker said. "The market is quiet."
The broker said the 10-year note auction could be the hardest of this week's $38.0 billion quarterly refunding for the market to digest.
That worry, and waiting for the Fed's beige book later today, could keep the market on the defensive, he said.
John Kadich said Thursday's 30-year bond auction was key.

"I would expect the auctions to go well and we should rally," Kadich said. "If we don't rally after tomorrow afternoon or Friday then that's telling me there's something wrong with the intermediate and long term trend," Kadich said.
If September does not rally to 115-20/32 or close above 115-8/32, "then my intermediate trend turns neutral to bearish," he said, putting targets at 112-24/32 to 113-8/32.
For the time being, September was stuck within Tuesday's range. Traders put minor resistance at Tuesday's 114-22/32 session high.
One T-bond futures trader said the market's tone was indecisive, and said without a move above 114-25/32 September was essentially directionless heading into the auction.
Tuesday's sale of three-year notes was largely as expected.

At 0812 CDT/1312 GMT, September T-bonds were down 1/32 to 114-18/32, notes fell 1/32 to 109-21/32, munis fell 3/32 to 120-10/32, Eurodollars rose 0.005 to 94.080. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
